# Ho-Smart v0.2.9 — Diagnostic privacy hardening

**Focus:** Protect sensitive receiver diagnostic data while preserving Home Assistant 2026.11.1 behavior.

## Why this release exists

Diagnostic exports could include raw hexadecimal representations of binary payloads and the contents of unparseable debug lines. Owner-facing captures should not disclose raw packets simply because they could not be decoded.

## What changed

- Binary payload captures now record byte length rather than raw hexadecimal content.
- Unparseable records now return only a redacted status and length, never the original line.
- Persisted debug journals and cloud checkpoints use owner-only permissions, including pre-existing log files when opened for append.
- Release publication now requires a successful validation run from this repository's main push, not a pull-request run.

## Limitations

This release cannot revoke old diagnostics already shared or copied outside Home Assistant. Existing on-disk logs are restricted as each file is opened; existing copies must be managed by their owners. Physical receiver write operations remain experimental.

## Upgrade instructions

Update using Home Assistant's integration manager or HACS/Marketplace, restart Home Assistant, and confirm events and diagnostic download. Existing devices, configuration entries, entity IDs and quiet-hours settings remain in place.
